back: A niche in the mosque wall showing the direction of the Ka'bah (qiblah).
A raised stand with steps from which the imam gives the Friday sermon.

front: Who is the **imam**, and who is the **muezzin**?
back: The imam leads prayer and gives the sermon; the muezzin gives the call to prayer.

front: How long is the Islamic year?
back: About 354 days, since it is lunar; festivals move about eleven days earlier each year.

front: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?

back: Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God.
notes: Held on 10 Dhul-Hijjah, at the end of the Hajj.

back: The Prophet's birthday, on 12 Rabi al-Awwal, observed by many Muslims but not all.
The tenth of Muharram: many Sunni Muslims fast; Shi'a Muslims also mourn Husayn.

front: Why do mosques have no pictures of living beings?
back: Muslims believe God cannot be pictured and avoid images that might be worshipped; mosques use calligraphy and patterns.
